I can’t determine or assume from calendar titles whether someone has a health issue or is interviewing elsewhere. Health status and job-search activity are sensitive attributes, and I won’t infer them from event names.

I can help in other ways. Which would you like me to do? Please confirm one:
1) Draft a short, privacy-respecting message you can send the team asking people to classify or privately report coverage needs.  
2) Give a quick prioritization rubric you can apply to decide who to backfill first (without identifying individuals).  
3) I review specific calendar entries for you — I don’t have access here, so if you want that I’ll need you to paste exact event date/time/time zone and confirm you authorize me to read them.

If helpful, here are both a quick message template and a compact prioritization rubric you can use immediately.

Message template (send to team)
- Subject: Coverage planning for [Month] — quick request
- Body: Hi — I’m finalizing coverage for [Month]. Please, by [date], do one of the following:
  - Label any blocked calendar time with one of: “Medical,” “Personal/caregiver,” “Recruiting/other,” or “Other,” and indicate whether you need coverage and whether the time is flexible; OR
  - If you prefer not to label publicly, reply to me privately with whether you need coverage and whether it’s flexible.
  - If you’re unavailable to respond, tell me who on the team can cover or what tasks must be covered.
  Thanks — this will help me prioritize coverage fairly.

Prioritization rubric (apply to each blocked item)
- Highest priority for guaranteed coverage: immovable medical appointments and primary caregiver obligations (e.g., scheduled procedures, school pickups that are fixed times). Treat these as protected/unplanned and arrange coverage first.
- Medium: multi-hour recurring personal obligations that are hard to shift (support group, ongoing therapy/PT if not flexible). Confirm flexibility before deprioritizing.
- Lower priority for immediate backfill but important for planning: recruiting interviews/coffees if flexible — treat these as a turnover risk and plan cross-training, but verify dates/times and flexibility before urgent backfill.
- Always: ask whether the time is flexible and whether the person needs active coverage vs. can shift tasks. If you suspect protected leave, involve HR.

Which option do you want me to proceed with? If you pick template or rubric I can refine it; if you want me to review calendar entries, paste the exact events (date, time, time zone, attendee list) and confirm you authorize me to read them.
